title: Rav Tuvi bar Kisni
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Shmuel’s student, as Hyman says we always find Rav Tuvi bar Kisna transmitting in Shmuel’s name, as in [Yevamot 40b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.40b.27), [Ketubot 64a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.64a.3), [Nedarim 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.12b.5), [Bava Batra 19b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.19b.7) and [Menachot 41a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.41a.17). There at [Menachot 70a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.70a.14), Rav Tavyomi bar Kisna transmits in Shmuel’s name. Hyman proposes reading Rav Tuvi bar Kisna, according to Dikdukei Soferim’s reading. There at [Menachot 76b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.76b.3), Rav Tuvi bar Kasna transmits in Shmuel’s name. Hyman proposes reading bar Kisna. In [Eruvin 104b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.104b.10), Rav Tavi bar Kisna transmits in Shmuel’s name. Hyman proposes reading Rav Tivi, and cites [Tosafot on Sotah 20b, s.v. Lo](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Sotah.20b.11.1).[^3]

notes.text: The heading’s Kisni (קיסני) is preserved in the title, while Kisna, Kasna, Tuvi, Tavyomi, Tavi and Tivi remain as the supplied body’s meaningful variants. Saved Davidson Menachot 70a/76b and Eruvin 104b retain several of those forms. The proposed corrections and always assertion remain Hyman’s, not global name harmonization.

The directly inspected Menachot 70a and Eruvin 104b occurrences read Tavyomi and Tavi respectively. The exact Dikdukei Soferim and Tosafot readings quoted here have not been independently inspected; those corrections remain Hyman’s.

The linked passages give Shmuel as the authority and vary the reporter’s name. In the consulted Tosafot on Sotah the citation reads Rav Tuvi bar Kisna. The directly linked Eruvin reads Rav Tavi bar Kisna. Menachot 70a has Tavyomi; 76b has Tuvi bar Kisna, where Hyman quotes Kasna. The printed Dikdukei Soferim reading is reported by Hyman.
